summary: The Zeekr 009 is a 5.2-metre battery-electric luxury people mover sold in three grades, from the single-motor 7-Seat FWD at $115,900 to the dual-motor 6-Seat AWD at $139,900 before on-road costs, which makes it the most expensive Chinese-built car in Australia and puts every grade over the luxury car tax threshold. CarExpert rates the cabin, equipment and surprising pace highly and calls the FWD the value pick, but measured 28.2kWh/100km against a 19.5kWh/100km claim and found the air suspension bouncy enough in Comfort mode to cause nausea. It undercuts the Mercedes-Benz EQV, but a young dealer network, a third row that cannot fold flat and very thin sales leave ownership and resale the open questions.
pros: The $115,900 7-Seat FWD keeps the full luxury cabin and the longest range in the line-up (604km WLTP from the same 116kWh pack), undercutting the Mercedes-Benz EQV 300 at $162,797 by more than $45,000
574L behind the third row measured to the lower window, against 333L in a Kia EV9 and 338L in a Hyundai Ioniq 9, so a full seven-seat load still leaves real luggage room

Equipment is limousine-grade on every grade: Nappa leather, 15.05-inch OLED centre screen, 17-inch rear entertainment screen, 30-speaker Yamaha audio, AR head-up display, heating/cooling fridge and dual-chamber air suspension; the $139,900 6-Seat AWD adds heated, ventilated, massaging second-row captain's chairs with fold-out tables
The 450kW dual-motor AWD grades run 0-100km/h in a claimed 4.5 seconds, and CarExpert found Sport mode tightens body control usefully for a 2,870kg van
Five-year unlimited-km warranty and roadside assistance, an 8-year/160,000km battery warranty, and capped-price servicing for eight years averaging $615 a year ($4,920 total) per CarExpert
cons: Every grade sits above the $91,661 fuel-efficient luxury car tax threshold, so buyers pay LCT and a novated lease gets no FBT exemption

CarExpert measured 28.2kWh/100km on the 6-Seat AWD, about 45 per cent worse than the 19.5kWh/100km claim, implying roughly 410km from a full charge rather than 582km; DC charging tops out at 150kW on Zeekr's AU page (205kW in its brochure), against up to 450kW on the sibling Zeekr 7X

CarExpert found Comfort mode bouncy enough to cause nausea, lane centring heavy-handed and driver monitoring over-sensitive, and the steering-wheel buttons and window switches feel cheap for the price

Practicality has limits: the third row cannot be removed or folded flat, payload is only 560kg on the AWD, no braked towing capacity is published, and the six-seat layout is not offered on the cheaper FWD

Resale and ownership are unproven: Zeekr has sold cars here only since 2024, CarExpert counts 123 009 sales in 2025 and 109 in 2026 to date, and the sibling Zeekr X was repriced down $5,000-$10,000 in one model year
